chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Barani and Uthman ibn Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Yazdad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from Hisham ibn Salim who said:

I spoke to a man in Medina from the tribe of Makhzum about the Imama. He said to me: So who is the Imam today? I said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad. He said to me: By Allah, I will tell him this! I said: This threat of his grieved me greatly for I was afraid that Abu Abdillah would curse me and disassociate from me. The Makhzumi went to him, entered to see him, and they began conversing. He said: He relayed to him the words of Hisham. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Have you not considered his words - for we are worthy of that? The man began crying and did not know what to say and had no words. He said: When the words of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to that man were reported to Hisham, he became happy and his grief abated.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.بَنِي مَخْزُومٍ: Banu Makhzum (a prominent tribe in Medina)

ai.seo_question: What happened when Hisham ibn Salim revealed the Imam's identity to a man from the Makhzum tribe?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Ikhtiyar* highlights the authority of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) in confirming the Imamate, illustrating the scholarly practice of verifying claims through direct consultation with the Imam. The anxiety of Hisham ibn Salim reflects the delicate balance between preserving the sanctity of the Imam's identity and the necessity of establishing legitimate leadership, a key theme in Shia political theology. The Imam’s response, 'Are we not the ones for that?', underscores the divine right and exclusive knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding their own succession.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/279] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Barani and Uthman b. Hamid from Muhammad b. Yazdad from Muhammad b. al-Husayn from al-Hajjal from Hisham b. Salim who said:

I debated a man in Madina from the tribe of Makhzum about the Imama. He [the man] said to me: so who is the Imam today then? I [Hisham] said: Ja’far b. Muhammad. He [the man] said to me: by Allah - I am going to tell him this! He [Hisham] said: this threat of his grieved me greatly for I was afraid that Abu Abdillah would curse me and disassociate from me [for divulging the secret of the Imama in the heat of the debate]. The Makhzumi went to him, entered in to see him and they began conversing. He [al-Hajjal] says: He [the Makhzumi] relayed to him the words of Hisham. Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: Have you not considered his words - for we are worthy of that [Imama]. The man began crying and did not know what to say and had no words [remained silent]. He [al-Hajjal] said: When the words of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام to that man were reported to Hisham he became happy and his grief abated.
